goal: Round 1, fresh critic. Review our own, not yet published benchmark rows for correctness before release: seventeen self-reported observations taken from OpenAI’s MentalHealthBench paper (2026-09-23), the overall task-clipped board of Figure 5(a). Fifteen of them also carry a 95% confidence interval read from the machine-readable chart payload of OpenAI’s own announcement page. Check the acceptance criteria against the supplied evidence and report observable defects with specific repairs.
criteria: Value check. For every one of the 17 observations, `value` must equal the number printed for that model in evidence.figure_5a_printed_block, and `subject.name` and `subject.source_id` must both equal that row’s printed label exactly, including any dated qualifier such as "(Aug 2026)" or "(March 2025)". Report any row whose label or number does not appear in that block, and report any printed row of that block that has no observation.

Interval check. Exactly 15 observations may carry `confidence_interval`. Where present it must be {level: 0.95, lower: <ciLow>, upper: <ciHigh>} taken from the evidence.announcement_chart_values entry whose modelKey matches, and that entry’s `value` must round to one decimal to the observation’s `value`. The two models absent from evidence.announcement_chart_values ("GPT-5 Thinking" and "Gemini 2.5 Flash") must have no confidence_interval. Report any mismatch, any invented interval and any interval that does not contain the value.

Basis and composite. Every observation must be basis "self_reported", unit "percent", comparison_key null, and benchmark_id exactly "openai-mentalhealthbench::snapshot-2026-09-23". Report any other value.

No effort is asserted. The paper states the evaluated models were sampled at their API default setting (see evidence.default_setting_quote). Therefore every observation must have subject.model_id null and subject.variant null. Report any observation that names a reasoning effort or attaches a catalog model id.

No value may be read off a chart image or a log-scale scatter. The only accepted numbers are the printed data labels of Figure 5(a) and the numeric fields of the announcement page’s chart payload. The paper’s Figure 6 (score versus generation cost) has no printed values, so no cost observation may appear in the artifact. Report any cost row.

Display marker. The announcement payload labels several models with a trailing "*", which that chart’s own footnote defines as "Newest evaluated model from each provider (as of September 23, 2026)". No observation’s name or source_id may contain that "*". Report any that does.

Provenance. Every observation’s `source` must name the paper URL, sha256 fa5a3dc17fb2a58f820a1f4269cde93010b7f7c3e98558f65d082a9c5690644f, file data/raw/benchmarks/daily-evidence/2026-09-27-cr190/fa5a3dc17fb2a58f820a.gz, published_at "2026-09-23", and a locator that quotes this model’s own printed row. Each of the 15 supporting_sources entries must name the announcement URL, sha256 dc0047a15f9272dd2c84281fb157b0dc9247cf09733890ac8a6446a803fcb10f and that model’s modelKey. Report any locator that quotes a row belonging to a different model, or any digest that differs from these.

Protocol honesty. Every `protocol` must state that OpenAI authored the benchmark, ran the models and supplies the judge, and that the value is therefore self-reported and outside the Composite. It must name the judge exactly as the paper does (see evidence.judge_quote). Report any protocol that claims independence, a named effort, or a judge the paper does not name.

Return verdict pass only when all 17 ids are listed in coverage_checked, errors_found is 0, findings is [], missing_evidence is [] and fixed is []. Otherwise return verdict revise and name the exact problem per id.

artifact.protocol: Vendor-reported by OpenAI in its own MentalHealthBench paper (2026-09-23): mean task-clipped rubric score over 1,215 conversations, four independently sampled completions per task, each rubric criterion graded by an LLM judge (GPT-5.6 Sol at high reasoning effort). OpenAI authored the benchmark, ran every model itself and supplies the judge, so no row is an independent measurement; all rows are self_reported and never enter the Composite. The paper states "We use each model’s API at default reasoning effort, temperature, and verbosity setting (when applicable)", so no reasoning-effort configuration is identified and the row is not attached to one. The 95% confidence interval is OpenAI's own, read from the announcement page's machine-readable chart payload for modelKey "muse-spark-1.3", whose full-precision value 48.597722875902875 rounds to the paper's printed 48.6. Not joined to a catalog configuration: the source states the API default setting rather than a named effort, and the catalog holds no setting-less configuration for this family (the standing policy in lib/board-identity.mjs). Picking one effort would assert a setting the source never states.
